newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Improved outlook for NZ CBDs - real estate review.
newsitem.headline: Improved outlook for NZ CBDs - real estate review.

text.p: Auckland and Wellington central business district office sectors continued to improve over 1996, consultants Ernst and Young said in their Real Estate Sector Review published on Friday.

Investment sales activity picked up in the second half after a slow start, confounding commentators who expected a subdued office investment market before the country's first MMP election in October, Ernst and Young said.
The formation of a National/New Zealand First coalition government would ensure there would not be any significant changes in economic direction.

"This backdrop, coupled with the forecast of stronger growth in the economy, lower interest rates and improving supply/demand balances in the office user market, suggests promising prospects for CBD office property over the medium to long term," real estate analyst Steve O'Malley said.

He said that by December 2001, the whole market vacancy rate is forecast to be just over five percent in Auckland, with the sub-prime market just under 3.0 percent. In Wellington, the rates were forecast to be 5.5 and 3.0 percent respectively.
The vacancy rate forecasts were driven by estimates of likely net office space absorption, which in turn were largely derived from the view of likely service sector employment growth.
Rental rates in both markets were forecast to continue increasing over the next five years in response to improving supply/demand balances.
By late 2001 Ernst and Young forecast rentals for prime quality space in Auckland at about NZ$445 per square metre and $440 in Wellington. CBD lease expiries showed a definite peak from 1997 to 2000.
